carousels.name: 'I'll quit p*rn when life calms down'

slides.title: "I'll quit p*rn when life calms down." [[Life won't calm down.]]
slides.sub: Why there's never a perfect time — and why that's fine.

slides.title: The [[perfect time]] myth
slides.body:
After exams. After this project. After the new year.

There's always a reason to keep p*rn around "for now."

slides.title: Stress is [[why]] you use it
slides.body: If you use p*rn to cope with stress, a stressful season is exactly when quitting matters most.

slides.title: Start [[messy]]
slides.body: You don't need a calm life to quit p*rn. You need one small step today. Messy starts still count.

slides.title: Start [[today]], not someday
items: Block p*rn right now — 2 minutes.
Pick one trigger to protect against this week.
Tell yourself: "Today is Day 1."
Expect it to be hard — and do it anyway.
slides.note: What "perfect time" have you been waiting for? Comment it 👇

slides.title:
The best time to quit p*rn?
[[Today.]]
slides.lead: Set up in minutes: a p*rn blocker, a panic button and a step-by-step recovery program.

carousels.name: In a relationship but still watching p*rn

slides.title: Happy relationship. [[Still can't stop watching p*rn.]]
slides.sub: Why a partner doesn't automatically cure p*rn addiction.

slides.title: It's [[not]] about them
slides.body: Many people still watch p*rn while loving their partner. That's a sign p*rn has become a coping habit, not a lack of love.

slides.title: Different [[need]]
slides.body: Stress, boredom, alone time at night — p*rn often fills moments a partner isn't part of. Find what those moments are.

slides.title: Secrecy [[grows]] distance
slides.body: Hiding p*rn from someone you love creates a wall — even if they never find out. You feel it, even if they don't.

slides.title: Protect your [[relationship]]
items: Notice when and why you turn to p*rn.
Invest in real intimacy and connection.
Consider honesty — with support if needed.
Get help to quit p*rn for good.
slides.note: Is this you right now? A simple "yes" helps others feel less alone 👇

slides.title:
Choose your partner
[[over p*rn.]]
slides.lead: 1-on-1 accountability, habit tracking your partner can see and an AI coach for the hard conversations.

carousels.name: Women struggle with p*rn addiction too

slides.title: P*rn addiction [[isn't just a guy thing.]]
slides.sub: Women struggle with it too — often in even more silence.

slides.title: More [[common]] than you think
slides.body: Studies of problematic p*rn use consistently include women. It's less talked about — not less real.

slides.title: Extra [[shame]]
slides.body: Because p*rn addiction is seen as a "male" problem, many women feel even more alone and ashamed. That silence makes it harder to get help.

slides.title: Same [[tools]] work
slides.body: Knowing your triggers, blocking p*rn, support and self-compassion help everyone. Recovery isn't gendered.

slides.title: If this is [[you]]
items: You're not strange or alone.
Block p*rn and know your triggers.
Find a safe space to talk — anonymous is fine.
Be kind to yourself — shame keeps the loop going.
slides.note: Share this so someone feels less alone 💬

slides.title:
P*rn recovery
[[for everyone.]]
slides.lead: A private, shame-free p*rn recovery app with an anonymous community — no names, no judgment.

carousels.name: Use the energy you get back from quitting p*rn

slides.title: Quit p*rn and feel restless? [[That's energy. Use it.]]
slides.sub: Where to put the drive many people say comes back.

slides.title: The [[restlessness]]
slides.body: Many people describe extra energy, restlessness or drive after quitting p*rn. If you don't direct it, it often turns back into urges.

slides.title: Into your [[body]]
slides.body: Training, sport, running, martial arts. Physical effort is one of the best outlets when p*rn urges feel loud.

slides.title: Into your [[goals]]
slides.body: The project you keep putting off. The skill you want. The business idea. Give the p*rn hours a mission.

slides.title: Channel it [[today]]
items: Pick one physical outlet for this week.
Pick one goal to work on daily.
Schedule both at your usual p*rn hours.
Track progress — watch it add up.
slides.note: Where are you putting your energy after quitting p*rn? 👇

slides.title:
Turn p*rn hours
[[into progress.]]
slides.lead: Daily actions, habit tracking and streaks to turn quitting p*rn into building something.

carousels.name: Wake up, grab phone, p*rn: the morning trap

slides.title: Wake up. Grab phone. [[Open p*rn.]] Sound familiar?
slides.sub: Why mornings can be a p*rn trap — and how to beat it.

slides.title: Half-[[awake]] autopilot
slides.body: Groggy, still in bed, phone in hand — your guard is down before your brain is fully on. Morning p*rn often happens on autopilot.

slides.title: A bad [[start]]
slides.body: Starting the day with p*rn can leave you with guilt and low energy for hours. Many people say the rest of the day goes downhill from there.

slides.title: Get [[up]] first
slides.body: The rule: feet on the floor before the phone is in your hand. Out of bed beats out of willpower.

slides.title: Your morning [[shield]]
items: Alarm across the room, not on your pillow.
Phone charges outside the bedroom.
P*rn blocker on 24/7, not just nights.
Water, light, movement — before any screen.
slides.note: Morning or night — when do p*rn urges hit you hardest? 👇

slides.title:
Win the morning
[[against p*rn.]]
slides.lead: A 24/7 p*rn blocker, daily actions for your morning and streaks that start the moment you wake up.
